title: Grade labels differ between school systems
statement: Before borrowing standards, texts or materials across school systems, check what each year or grade label means there, since the same number can name different ages.
example: England's Year 9 is normally ages 13–14, while US Grade 9 is typically ages 14–15.
detail: Curriculum notes comparing four frameworks for a course whose own specification calls it both Grade 9 and Year 9 (`g9/library/text/L9b6d99.txt`, lines 1 and 4) open with the rule not to merge year labels or frameworks (`g9/library/collections/codex-2026-10-02-curriculum-research/GRADE9-CURRICULUM-OPTIONS.md`, line 5). England's Year 9 is normally ages 13–14 and within Key Stage 3, so it is not the age-equivalent label for US Grade 9, typically ages 14–15 (lines 7-9). A second note, on pandemic-era cases, repeats that the labels should not be treated as interchangeable (`g9/library/collections/codex-2026-10-02-curriculum-research/COVID-ERA-TEACHING-EVIDENCE.md`, line 21).

evidence.quote: England Year 9 is normally ages 13–14 and is within KS3; it is not the age-equivalent label for US Grade 9.
Year 9 in England is normally ages 13–14; US Grade 9 is typically ages 14–15. The labels should not be treated as interchangeable.
Do not merge year labels or frameworks
This document is the build specification for the Year 9 ELA app
